title: Mediterranean Stuffed Peppers
summary:
Prep: 10 minutes | Cook: 1hr 15 minutes | Total: 1hr 25 minutes
Yield: 8 servings | Serving Size: 1/2 stuffed pepper

Ingredients
• 2 tsp finely crushed rosemary leaves
• 1 tsp cinnamon
• 1 tsp oregano
• 1/2 tsp salt
• 1 pound lean ground beef
• 1 can (14 ounces) no salt added tomato sauce
• 1/4 cup toasted slivered almonds
• 1 cup cooked brown rice
• 1 egg, beaten
• 4 medium bell peppers
• 1/2 cup crumbled reduced fat feta cheese

Directions
1. Preheat oven to 375°F.
2. Cook ground beef in large skillet on medium-high heat for 5 to 7 minutes or until no longer pink, stirring occasionally to break up meat. Drain fat. Season with rosemary, cinnamon, oregano and salt.
3. Stir in tomato sauce and almonds. Bring to a boil. Remove from heat. Add rice and egg; mix well.
4. Cut bell peppers in half, lengthwise. Remove stem and seeds.
5. Arrange bell pepper halves, cut-side up, in 13x9-inch baking dish. Spoon beef mixture evenly into bell pepper halves. Pour 1/4 cup water into baking dish. Cover with foil.
6. Bake for 45 minutes or until bell peppers are tender.
7. Sprinkle filling with feta cheese. Bake, uncovered, 12 to 15 minutes longer or until cheese is lightly browned.

Nutrition Facts Per Serving: Calories: 225 | Carbohydrates: 24.6g | Protein: 16.9g | Fat: 6.8g | Saturated Fat: 2.3g | Fiber: 3.1g | Sodium: 290mg

title: Lemony Lentil & Salmon Salad
summary:
Prep: 15 minutes I Cook: 0 minutes I Total: 15 minutes
Yield: 3 servings I Serving Size: 1 salad ("'2 cups)

Ingredients
2 tablespoons lemon juice (about½ lemon)
2 tablespoons canola or olive oil
2 teaspoons dried dill or parsley (or 1 tablespoon fresh)
1 teaspoon mustard (about one 0.25-ounce packet)
¼ teaspoon onion powder
¼ teaspoon garlic powder
¼ teaspoon ground black pepper
1 (15-ounce) can lentils, drained and rinsed
1 (5-ounce) can boneless skinless salmon in water, drained
1 cup diced or sliced vegetables (one type or combination;
e.g. bell pepper, carrots, cucumber, onion)
4 cups salad greens (about one 5-ounce container), divided

Directions
1. In a large mixing bowl, use a fork to whisk together
the lemon juice, oil, dill or parsley, mustard, onion
powder, garlic powder, and black pepper (see
Recipe Notes).
2. Add the lentils, salmon, and selected vegetables.
Stir to combine.
3. Divide the salad greens between three plates or
bowls (¾ cup each), followed by the lentil-salmon
mixture (~1¼ cups each).
4. Serve cold

Recipe Notes
• A storebought salad dressing can be used, if desired. Simply skip step 1 and add¼ cup to the mixture in step 2.
• For a make-ahead version, consider using coleslaw mix in place of the salad greens. Add to the mixture in step 2,
then serve or refrigerate for up to 4 days.
• Canned tuna or chicken can be used in place of the canned salmon, if desired.

Nutrition Facts Per Serving: Calories: 335 I Total Fat: 12.5 g I Saturated Fat: 2 g | Sodium: 210 mg I Total Carbohydrate: 34.5 g I Dietary Fiber: 13.5 g I Protein: 27 g

title: BBQ Meatloaf Muffins
summary:
Prep: 15 minutes | Cook: 40 minutes | Total: 55 minutes
Yield: 9 servings | Serving Size: 1 muffin

Ingredients
• 1 package (~1.25 lbs) 99% lean ground turkey breast
• 1/2 cup oats (ground) or bread crumbs (~1 slice whole grain bread)
• 1 cup onion, finely diced
• 1 large egg
• 2 Tbsp Worcestershire sauce
• 1/2 cup Ray’s No Sugar Added BBQ Sauce, plus extra for topping
• 1/4 tsp salt
• Fresh ground pepper, to taste
• 1/2 tsp garlic powder (optional)
• Non-stick cooking spray

Directions
1. Preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. Coat 12-cup muffin tin with non-stick cooking spray
3. Grind oats in food processor/blender, or toast 1 slice whole grain bread, let cool, then grind into breadcrumbs
4. Finely chop or process onion and add to a large mixing bowl
5. Combine turkey, bread crumbs, onion, egg, Worcestershire, BBQ sauce and seasonings
6. Mix well with hands or large spoon
7. Add meatloaf mixture to fill 9 muffin cups, flattening out the tops
8. Top each muffin with ~1/2 Tbsp BBQ sauce
9. Bake for ~40 minutes until done

Recipe Notes
• Add additional herbs/spices to meet your preference (rosemary, thyme, etc.)
• Bake in a mini muffin tin if smaller portions are desired

title: At the Table: DHS resources that help Veterans build a future in homeland security
summary:
Across the country, many Veterans are choosing homeland security as their next mission. The leadership, discipline, and technical skills Veterans developed in uniform translate naturally to work that protects the nation’s people, borders, infrastructure, and waterways. As the Department of Homeland Security undergoes major modernization efforts and expands its workforce, Veterans are stepping forward as the next generation of national security professionals.

In the latest episode of At the Table, VA Deputy Secretary Paul R. Lawrence, Ph.D., talks with Deputy Secretary of Homeland Security Troy Edgar about the opportunities available to Veterans at DHS. Their conversation highlights why Veterans are well prepared for careers in homeland security, how DHS is growing across multiple mission areas, and what resources are available to help Veterans navigate the transition.

Deputy Secretary Edgar explains that DHS currently has almost 30,000 open positions across 23 mission components. These components include law enforcement, maritime security, emergency management, cybersecurity, transportation security, and immigration services. Approximately 30 percent of DHS’s 260,000 employees are already Veterans. DHS has long recognized that Veterans bring mission focus, teamwork, responsibility, and an ability to perform under pressure. A career at DHS allows many Veterans to continue serving their country in a new capacity. 

Veterans can explore these opportunities at the DHS careers site: https://www.dhs.gov/homeland-security-careers.
